message.content: The kernel and contract are already fully in context. The chief risk is the fp16 round-trip of softmax probabilities (line 15) combined with the input generator's deliberate cancellation (V recentered by 0.9·(p@v)), which shrinks the reference output norm and tightens the E budget. I'll record the directly testable, in-scope claim for the Experimenter to probe.

function.arguments: {"rationale": "The kernel rounds softmax probabilities to fp16 (relative error ~2^-11) before the weighted V sum, and make_inputs deliberately recenters V by 0.9*(p@v) so the reference output is small via cancellation; the resulting absolute error scaled by max(||ref||, 0.001*sqrt(32)) may exceed the 0.001 relative budget on this exact workload.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Contract: E = ||output-reference||_2 / max(||reference||_2, 0.001*sqrt(#outputs)) <= 0.001 on the exact make_inputs() workload (seed 815, N=128, D=32, K scaled 1.9, V recentered 0.9*(p@v)); reference is the operation in float64 on the same float32 inputs."}, {"source": "kernel.py lines 15, 38-43", "summary": "Line 15 quantizes p to fp16; make_inputs' V recentering (v -= 0.9*(p@v)) engineers output cancellation, so this exact fixed workload is the case the budget applies to."}], "statement": "On the single seed-815 workload (N=128, D=32), the kernel's fp16 rounding of softmax probabilities (line 15) causes E = ||out - ref||_2 / max(||ref||_2, 0.001*sqrt(32)) to exceed 0.001, violating the contract's compliance budget."}
